record.original_question: In the binary case, give an improvement of the result of Lemma 10 in the paper.

evidence.quote: In the binary case, give an improvement of the result of Lemma 10 in the paper.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let A be a finite alphabet and A* the free monoid of finite words over A, with empty word ε. A finite word p ∈ A* is a palindrome if it equals its reversal. The palindromic length of a finite word w ∈ A*, denoted PL(w), is the least integer k ≥ 0 such that w can be written as a concatenation w = p_1 p_2 ⋯ p_k of palindromes p_i ∈ A* (with PL(ε) = 0).

A central conjecture in this area asserts that every infinite word x ∈ A^ℕ for which the set {PL(u) : u is a finite factor of x} is bounded must be ultimately periodic. The standard quantitative tool in the partial results toward this conjecture is a lemma of the following form:

(*) There exist functions N, M : ℤ_{>0} → ℤ_{>0} such that, for every alphabet A, every k ≥ 1, and every finite word w ∈ A* with |w| ≥ N(k), if every factor of w has palindromic length at most k, then w contains a factor of the form u^{M(k)} with u ∈ A* nonempty (in particular w contains an M(k)-th power).

Concretely, the established bound takes the shape N(k) ≤ F(k), M(k) ≥ G(k) for explicit increasing functions F, G arising from a counting/Ramsey-type argument on positions of palindromic factorizations.

Problem. Restrict to the binary alphabet A = {0, 1}. Provide an improvement of the quantitative bounds in (*) in this binary case: that is, exhibit functions N_2(k) and M_2(k) such that the statement (*) holds for A = {0, 1} with N replaced by N_2 and M replaced by M_2, where N_2 grows strictly slower than the currently known F (respectively M_2 grows strictly faster than the currently known G), and prove the corresponding result.
artifact.status_search_result: The overarching Frid–Puzynina–Zamboni conjecture (bounded palindromic length implies ultimate periodicity) remains open as of recent literature; partial results have been extended (Sturmian words by Frid 2018, words with many periodic palindromes 2020, Sierpinski word 2022). No source explicitly verifying or refuting an improvement of the specific auxiliary "Lemma 10" quantitative bound in the binary case was located in the search.

status_evidence.title: Palindromic Length of Words with Many Periodic Palindromes
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the Frid–Puzynina–Zamboni conjecture and proves it in further special cases.
status_evidence.claim: The general conjecture surrounding palindromic length remains open, with continued partial progress.

status_evidence.title: On Palindromic Length of Sturmian Sequences
status_evidence.snippet: Frid (2018) proved limsup pal_u(n) = +∞ for any Sturmian word.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress is ongoing; full conjecture still open.

status_evidence.title: On palindromic factorization of words
status_evidence.snippet: Frid, Puzynina, Zamboni (2013) introduced palindromic length and proved bounded palindromic length forces k-powers; basis for the lemma to be improved.
status_evidence.claim: Original quantitative lemma whose binary improvement is sought.
